spans.text: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kurus together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants when he arrived at a town of the Kurus named Thullakoṭṭhika.
He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

spans.text: Yathā bhagavā aññāsi: When he knew that “abhabbo kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattitun”ti, atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ raṭṭhapālaṁ etadavoca: it was impossible for Raṭṭhapāla to resign the training and return to a lesser life, he said, “yassadāni tvaṁ, raṭṭhapāla, kālaṁ maññasī”ti.

spans.text: Yathā bhagavā aññāsi: When he knew that “abhabbo kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattitun”ti, atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ raṭṭhapālaṁ etadavoca: it was impossible for Raṭṭhapāla to resign the training and return to a lesser life, he said, “yassadāni tvaṁ, raṭṭhapāla, kālaṁ maññasī”ti.
He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”
“Sir, I would like to visit my parents, if the Buddha allows it.”
Then the Buddha focused on encompassing Raṭṭhapāla’s mind.
